I checked the code: Extract log's success notification already names the destination note and section. So the request is already partly met. I can't write firm requirements until the owner says what's missing (Q1 below).

## What the code does now (answers the owner's reply)

- **Success notice.** After the target note is written and the source is updated, it shows `Extract log: moved child block to "<target basename>" > <section text>` for 4 seconds (`src/commands/extractLog.ts:168-171`, `src/config.ts:15`).
  - The note is shown by its file name only (no folder or `.md`), in quotes.
  - The section is the configured log heading (default `## Log`) with the `#`s removed, so you see `Log` (`extractLog.ts:116`, `src/utils/tasks.ts:20-31`).
- **What the notice leaves out:**
  - The new dated sub-heading the content actually goes under, e.g. `### [[2026-11-09 Mon]] Checkin mit Chris` (`extractLog.ts:117-119`, inserted at `:158-160`).
  - Whether the `## Log` section already existed or was just added at the end of the file (`tasks.ts:253-271`).
  - The note's folder. Two notes with the same name look identical.
  - That the content was also copied to the clipboard. That copy happens silently and fails silently (`extractLog.ts:17-29`, `:72-75`).
  - It is plain text with no link to click.
- **Other notices:**
  - "No children" (`extractLog.ts:63`)
  - "No listItems metadata" (`extractLog.ts:57`)
  - "No wikilink found" (`extractLog.ts:109`)
  - A catch-all error shown for 8 seconds (`extractLog.ts:173-176`, `config.ts:20`)
- **Tests.** Nothing checks the success notice's text. The integration tests only check the "No children" and error notices (`tests/integration/extractLog.plugin.test.ts:43,362`). The test helper does record every notice (`tests/helpers/extractLogPluginTestHelper.ts:170-206`).
- **Similar command.** Complete project task's notice uses wikilink style: `Task completed and logged to [[Migration Initiative]].` (`tests/integration/completeProjectTask.plugin.test.ts:329-331`).

## Intended outcome (requirement)
After a successful Extract log, the notification tells the user where the content went, clearly enough that they don't need to open the target note to check.

## Questions that block progress
1. **What's missing from today's notice?** It already names the note and section. Which of these should be added?
   a. The dated sub-heading, e.g. `"Migration Initiative" > Log > [[2026-11-09 Mon]] Checkin mit Chris`
   b. The folder or full path, so same-named notes can be told apart
   c. A note when the Log section was just created
   d. That the content was copied to the clipboard
   e. A clickable link to the new spot
   f. Only rewording (for example, matching Complete project task's `[[Note]]` style)
   Also: could the user be on an older version that doesn't show this notice yet?
2. **If (e) is wanted:** a clickable notice adds UI behaviour and needs Obsidian code in `src/adapters/`. Is that in scope, or should the notice stay plain text?
3. **Should the notice stay visible longer than 4 seconds?** That's the shared success timeout, so changing it for every command is a separate decision.

## Assumptions (please confirm or correct)
- Only the wording or content of the success notice changes. Where content is inserted, the source link rewrite and the error notices stay the same.
- The notice is still shown only after both the target note and the source note have been updated.
- Users don't need a new setting for this.

## Acceptance cases (draft, to fill in once Q1 is answered)
- **Named link.** Extracting from `- Checkin mit Chris zu [[Migration Initiative]]` with children gives a notice naming `Migration Initiative`, the Log section, and whatever extra detail Q1 picks.
- **Bare link bullet.** For a bullet that's only a link (`- [[Project]]`), the notice reflects the heading built from the parent bullet.
- **Missing Log section.** If the target note has no Log section, the notice is accurate, and says the section was created if Q1(c) is chosen.
- **Custom heading.** With the log heading set to `### Inbox`, the notice says `Inbox`.
- **Unchanged cases.** No children → "No children" notice and no notice naming a destination. A failed write → error notice only.

## High-level plan
1. Write integration tests first that pin the exact success text in `tests/integration/extractLog.plugin.test.ts`, using the helper's `notice` field.
2. Move the message building into a pure helper in `src/utils/notices.ts`, next to `formatTransferNotice`, with unit tests. Its inputs would be the note name, section text, and the optional details chosen in Q1.
3. Call that helper from `extractLog.ts:168`. If the "section created" detail is wanted, `insertBlockAfterHeading` would need to report that back.
4. Add a CHANGELOG entry written from the user's point of view.

# Requirements handoff (revision 2): ticking a task in a weekly, monthly or yearly note cascades it down to today's daily Log

## Intended outcome
When you tick a task `[x]` in a weekly, monthly or yearly note, the task moves down one level at a time until it reaches today's daily note. It ends up there completed, under `dailyNoteLogHeading` (default `## Log`), not under Todo. Every note it passes through, including the one you ticked in, keeps it as `[<]` (Scheduled). After this, weekly, monthly and yearly notes never hold a completed task. The `[<]` markers and wikilinks are the paper trail.

## What the owner's replies settled
- **The push cascades, it doesn't skip levels (correction).** Yearly goes to this month, then this week, then today. Monthly goes to this week, then today. Weekly goes to today. This is the same chain push task down already uses (`src/utils/periodicNotes.ts:396-428`). It replaces requirement 4 from revision 1.
- **Q1, ticking in a note whose period doesn't include today → (b).** The task stays `[x]` where it is and a notice explains why. Push task down already refuses in this case (`src/commands/pushTaskDown.ts:73-77`), and `getLowerNotePath` throws (`periodicNotes.ts:402-404`).
- **Q2, a ticked subtask → (a).** Only the ticked task moves, with its own children as in A4. Its parent stays open in the source.
- **Q3, project tasks.** These are also logged in the project note, under a link back to **the daily note**, the same way daily-note ticks work today (`src/events/autoMoveCompleted.ts:203-228`, `src/adapters/projectCompletion.ts`).

## Firm requirements
1. The trigger is a change *to* `[x]` in a weekly, monthly or yearly note, in any section.
2. The source line becomes `[<]`. It is not deleted.
3. Each in-between note (this month, this week) gets the task, which then becomes `[<]` there too.
4. Today's daily note gets the task as `[x]` under `dailyNoteLogHeading`.
5. If today isn't inside the source note's period: nothing moves, the line stays `[x]`, and a notice appears.
6. A ticked subtask moves on its own; its parent stays open.
7. A project task is logged once, in the project note, under the daily note's link.
8. Daily notes behave exactly as they do now (`autoMoveCompleted.ts:169`).

## Open questions (they block implementation)
1. **How the task appears in the in-between notes.** My assumption is that it goes under `periodicNoteTaskTargetHeading` (`## Todo`) as `[<]`, which is what two push-downs in a row would leave. Is that right, or should those notes hold no copy at all? If they hold none, the "cascade" only exists in the links.
2. **A matching task already in the in-between note.** Push task down merges into a matching open task (`pushTaskDown.ts:151-156`). In a cascade, merging would turn the existing task `[<]` and send *its* children down to the daily note. Options:
   - (a) merge as push down does;
   - (b) always insert a separate `[<]` line;
   - (c) something else.

## Assumptions (please correct any that are wrong)
- **A1.** It runs automatically in the existing tick handler. There is no new command, and the "Complete project task" command counts as a tick.
- **A2.** Started tasks (`[/]`) are left alone. Lines that are already `[<]`, `[>]` or `[x]` and just get edited don't trigger it.
- **A3.** Children follow push-down rules: open children move with the task, and finished subtrees stay in the source (`pushTaskDown.ts:139-140`, `166-170`).
- **A4.** For a project task, the children go to the project log, and only the task line itself lands in the daily Log. This mirrors `moveLineOnly` (`autoMoveCompleted.ts:204-209`).
- **A5.** Missing in-between notes, a missing daily note and a missing heading are all created (`getOrCreateFile`, the existing heading-creation behaviour).
- **A6.** Writes go from the bottom up: daily note (and project note) first, then the in-between notes, and the source edit last, after the "line unchanged" check. If a write fails, the source stays `[x]` and an error notice appears. Notes that were already written are not rolled back.
- **A7.** Unticking afterwards doesn't reverse anything.

## Acceptance cases
| # | Given | When | Then |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | This week's weekly note: `- [ ] Call Sam` | tick it | weekly: `- [<] Call Sam`; today's daily Log: `- [x] Call Sam` |
| 2 | This month's monthly note | tick a task | monthly `[<]` → this week's note `[<]` (Q1, Q2) → daily Log `[x]` |
| 3 | This year's yearly note | tick a task | yearly `[<]` → month `[<]` → week `[<]` → daily Log `[x]` |
| 4 | Last week's weekly note, or next month's monthly note | tick a task | stays `[x]` in place; notice shown; no other note changes |
| 5 | Nested subtask under an open parent | tick the subtask | subtask cascades; parent stays `[ ]` in the source |
| 6 | Task with one open child and one completed child | tick it | open child travels with it; completed child stays under the `[<]` line |
| 7 | `[[Project]] Draft memo` in the weekly note | tick it | `[<]` in weekly; `[x]` in daily Log; one project-log entry under the daily note's link |
| 8 | Today's daily note, or this week's note, doesn't exist | tick in the monthly note | the missing notes are created and the cascade completes |
| 9 | `[/]` set in the weekly note | — | nothing happens |
| 10 | Daily note | tick a task in Todo | unchanged from today's behaviour |
| 11 | Writing to the daily note fails | tick in the weekly note | source stays `[x]`; error notice shown |
| 12 | The in-between week already has a matching open task | tick in the monthly note | **depends on Q2** |

## Implementation plan (high level)
1. **Pure logic in `src/utils/` (unit tests first).**
   - Build the cascade path by calling `getLowerNotePath` repeatedly until it returns `daily`.
   - Build the payload to transfer (`getTransferableChildren` / `prepareTaskContentForTarget`).
   - Work out the in-between insert-then-`[<]` edit (after Q1 and Q2 are answered).
   - Work out the daily Log insertion (`findLogInsertionLine`, plus the heading-creation branch of `computeAutoMove`).
2. **Routing in `autoMoveCompleted.ts`.** Replace the daily-only check at `:169`. Daily notes keep the current path. Other periodic notes first check `dateIsInPeriod`, then write bottom-up with `vault.process`, then update the source after the re-read check. Project tasks reuse `completeProjectTaskAtLine` with the daily note as the link source.
3. **Integration tests** for the cases above, following `tests/CLAUDE.md`.
4. **Docs.** Add a CHANGELOG entry ("Ticking a task in a weekly/monthly/yearly note files it down to today's daily log"), and update the heading-settings table in CLAUDE.md and the header comment in `autoMoveCompleted.ts`.
